about: The Epistle of the formulary “Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Behold, he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills. My beloved is like a roe and a young deer. See, he himself stands behind our wall, looking in through the windows, looking out through the lattices. See, my beloved speaks to me: Arise, make haste, my love, my dove, my beautiful one, and come. For the winter has now passed; the rain has gone away and withdrawn. Flowers have appeared in our land; the season of pruning has arrived; the voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land; the fig tree has brought forth its green figs; the vines in blossom have yielded their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come. My dove in the holes in the rock, in the hollow of the wall, show me your face, let your voice sound in my ears; for your voice is sweet, and your face is comely.
